**Finding: Deviation (GOVLAW — medium severity)**

The governing law provision sits at Section 20(h) (General Matters, para p0146):

> "(h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia."

**Why it deviates:** Nova Scotia / Canadian law with Nova Scotia courts is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales). It is also Garman's likely home jurisdiction, so both law and venue favour the counterparty. I confirmed there is no arbitration clause anywhere in the Agreement, so the only issue is the choice of law and court.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** minimal word-level substitution to New York law and exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, keeping the sentence structure intact. The comment offers the playbook fallbacks (Delaware/California, or England and Wales with London courts) in case Garman resists New York.
